key_insight: An automated AI pipeline can curate CMR reports and images end-to-end to diagnose multiple cardiac diseases with strong performance, especially when models and modalities are ensembled.
clinical_relevance: This could help speed up and standardize interpretation of conventional CMR studies, potentially supporting clinicians in identifying cardiomyopathy and cardiac amyloidosis.
method: Used open-source local LLMs to extract diagnostic labels from narrative CMR reports.
Preprocessed multimodal CMR data, including cine and late gadolinium enhancement (LGE) sequences.
Fine-tuned three vision foundation models (DINO, VST, UMedPT) in a two-stage training approach.
evidence_signal: The approach was trained on 988 curated cases and evaluated on an independent test set of 1067 patients, with ensemble AUCs reaching 0.959 for HCM and 0.966 for cardiac amyloidosis.
watch_item: Performance is promising, but real-world deployment still depends on external validation, workflow integration, and consistent data quality across sites.
paper_title: Development of an automated, reliable, and clinically meaningful artificial intelligence (AI) tool for diagnosing cardiac disease from conventional cardiovascular magnetic resonance (CMR) images
